As concerns mount over the impact of hikes in fuel prices on the economy, Permanent Secretary to the Treasury Ramathan Ggoobi maintains that Uganda remains secure in terms of fuel supply, noting that the country’s fuel partners, Vitol, operate a diversified global refinery network capable of sustaining supply.
He however, acknowledges that global crude oil prices have risen due to the ongoing conflict, describing the situation as a temporary external shock.
Ggoobi further points to what government sees as a long-term cushion for the economy, with Uganda expected to commence oil production this year, alongside ongoing efforts to construct a 60,000-barrel-per-day refinery aimed at strengthening the country’s energy security and reducing reliance on imported petroleum products.
